answer: The oasis graph is validated at intake and the gale frontier is published, thus the ancestry of every answer is public, and haven anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Every submission must name 3 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight. A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 153 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
